problem: To prove a lower bound on the variance-scaled normalized Turán (log-concavity) deficit at the first-descent index of a Poisson-binomial pmf, namely V(1 - f_{D-1}f_{D+1}/f_D^2) >= 1/4 whenever V >= 1.
debate: The literature on quantitative log-concavity and mode behaviour of Bernoulli sums and real-rooted coefficient sequences: Newton's inequalities, Hillion and Johnson's ultra-log-concavity bounds, Johnson's p-dependent bound, Darroch's mode theorem, and the maximal-mass bounds of Bobkov, Marsiglietti and Melbourne.
gap: Existing lower bounds on the Turán deficit scale with n or with the success probabilities, so they degenerate when summands with p_i near 0 or 1 pile up at fixed variance, and the mode-location and maximal-mass results do not control the deficit at all.
contribution: A variance-only bound V*delta_D >= 1/4 (for V >= 1) with a corollary of geometric decay f_{D+r}/f_D <= exp(-r/(4V)) past the mode, a binomial family showing the best constant is at most 1/3, and a proof that is partly computer-assisted (exact Bernstein expansions on a compact range).
note: The statement is clean and the gap is stated plainly, but the only motivation on the page is a question you set yourself, so name a concrete result that needs a variance-only Turán deficit at the mode or referees will read this as a computer-checked inequality whose constant you have not settled (1/4 against 1/3).
